Title: Congress Passes Bill Requiring All Laws To Be Written In Arial Font Size 12
Subtitle: Bipartisan agreement reached after 14-hour debate over whether Comic Sans 'sends the right message'
Body:
WASHINGTON — In a rare display of bipartisan unity that has left political analysts stunned and slightly confused, the United States Congress passed the Federal Legislative Typography Standardization Act Thursday, mandating that all future legislation must be written exclusively in Arial font at a precise size of 12 points.

The bill, which passed 387-48 in the House and 92-8 in the Senate, comes after a landmark 14-hour floor debate that devolved at multiple points into shouting matches over the appropriateness of Comic Sans.

"The American people deserve laws they can read clearly, and clearly, Times New Roman has had its day," said House Speaker Mike Jenkins (R-OH), who reportedly spent three weeks workshopping the phrase before delivering it. "This is about dignity. This is about clarity. This is about fonts."

"I've been in the Senate 22 years and I've never seen both sides agree on anything. Now we've agreed that Papyrus is an abomination." — Sen. Diane Holloway (D-CA)

The bill does include a controversial rider that bans the use of Papyrus in any government document, a provision that was added at the last minute and credited with securing the final 12 votes needed for passage.

President Biden is expected to sign the bill into law later this week, using a pen loaded with 12-point Arial ink.
Author: The Bunion Staff
ImageAlt: The United States Capitol building with a large Arial font 'A' projected onto it

Title: Area Man Convinced He Could Have Played In The NFL If He'd Just Tried A Little Harder
Subtitle: Local accountant, 44, believes his brief JV career proves he 'had the raw talent'
Body:
DAYTON, OH — Local accountant and father of three Derek Holt, 44, remains firmly convinced that a professional football career was well within his reach had he simply applied himself more during his two seasons on the Westview High School junior varsity squad in 1997 and 1998.

"I had the hands. I had the vision. I just didn't have the system around me," said Holt, who recorded zero receptions across both seasons and was moved to third-string kicker after repeatedly lining up on the wrong side of the ball.

Holt, who stands 5'9" and describes his current fitness level as "a work in progress," says the dream was stolen from him by a combination of bad luck, poor coaching, and an overly demanding AP Chemistry class that met during the same period as film study.

"Patrick Mahomes is good, don't get me wrong. But he had advantages I just didn't have. Did he ever have to memorize the krebs cycle? I don't think so."

His wife, Karen Holt, declined to comment for this story. His teenage son rolled his eyes for an extended period before leaving the room.

According to sources close to Holt, he has repeated some version of this belief at every Thanksgiving dinner since 2003, most recently supplementing it with a detailed analysis of how he "basically invented" the read-option.
Author: Chad Watkins
ImageAlt: A man in business casual attire holding a football in a park

Title: Nation's Scientists Achieve Breakthrough In Understanding Where All The Tupperware Lids Go
Subtitle: New quantum physics theory suggests lids exist in 'superposition between kitchen drawer and oblivion'
Body:
CAMBRIDGE, MA — Researchers at MIT's Institute for Applied Household Mysteries announced Monday a landmark breakthrough in one of science's most vexing unsolved problems: the systematic disappearance of Tupperware lids from American homes at a rate that has no plausible physical explanation.

The team, led by Dr. Patricia Nguyen, published their findings in the journal Nature Domestic, proposing what they call the "Lid Displacement Hypothesis" — a theory suggesting that plastic container lids exist in a quantum superposition between their observed location ("the second shelf") and a parallel dimension they have termed "The Junk Drawer Plane."

"We have nine containers and three lids. We started with a matching set," said Dr. Nguyen. "The math doesn't work. It has never worked. We needed to understand why."

"Our models suggest lids do not disappear randomly. They disappear precisely when you have leftovers you actually want to save." — Dr. Patricia Nguyen

The breakthrough came after researchers installed cameras in 200 American kitchens and monitored lid movement for 18 months. The findings were unambiguous: lids are consistently present when conducting an inventory and consistently absent when needed.

The team is now working on a follow-up study addressing where all the good pens go and why there are 14 phone chargers but none of them fit any current device.
Author: Dr. Pamela Kroft
ImageAlt: A pile of mismatched Tupperware containers with no lids

Title: Local Restaurant Now Charging $47 For What Used To Be Called A 'Hamburger'
Subtitle: Menu describes item as 'Artisanal Heritage Beef Medallion on a Hand-Crafted Semolina Landing Pad'
Body:
BROOKLYN, NY — Customers of the newly opened Fortnight Bistro were reportedly baffled Thursday upon discovering that the establishment's signature entrée — described on the menu as the "Artisanal Heritage Beef Medallion presented on a Hand-Crafted Semolina Landing Pad with a Seasonal Condiment Suite" — is, in fact, a hamburger priced at $47.

"I ordered it because I didn't know what it was," admitted local graphic designer Tyler Baines, 31, who described the dish as arriving on a small wooden board alongside a "sad little cup of ketchup." "It was a burger. It was a $47 burger."

The restaurant's owner and executive chef, Marcus DuPont, defended the pricing in an interview conducted entirely in the restaurant's "ambient soundscape zone," which appears to be a corner with a speaker playing field recordings.

"People don't understand the provenance," said DuPont, 34. "The beef is from a single cow named Gerald who was raised on a regenerative farm and, according to our supplier, 'died doing what he loved.' That has value."

"The brioche bun is baked fresh daily using a sourdough starter that dates to 1987. We feel that is worth $12 on its own." — Chef Marcus DuPont

The restaurant received 4.2 stars on Yelp, with most reviewers calling the burger "genuinely excellent" and "not worth $47."
Author: The Bunion Staff
ImageAlt: An elaborately presented hamburger on a wooden board

Title: New Study Finds 9 Out Of 10 Studies Are Made Up To Support Pre-Existing Conclusions
Subtitle: Researchers stress the 10th study, which is theirs, is completely legitimate
Body:
BOSTON — A new study published Tuesday in the Journal of Research About Research has found that approximately 90% of all scientific studies are reverse-engineered from a conclusion the researchers had already decided upon before collecting a single data point.

The study, conducted by a team of researchers who stress repeatedly that their study is "definitely in the other 10 percent," surveyed 1,200 academic papers across 14 disciplines and found that in a majority of cases, the data appeared to have been "helpfully nudged" toward a predetermined outcome through a process the paper diplomatically terms "selective enthusiasm."

"The findings are striking," said lead researcher Dr. Alan Morse, who noted that he began the study already knowing what it would find. "We set out to prove that studies are unreliable, and we succeeded. We consider this a victory for science."

"Correlation doesn't imply causation, but it does imply a publishable paper and a grant extension, which is nearly as good." — Dr. Alan Morse

The study has already been cited in 14 other studies, nine of which use it to support conclusions that the original data does not actually support.

When reached for comment, the scientific community issued a joint statement noting that while the findings were "deeply concerning," further research was clearly needed before any conclusions could be drawn, and requested additional funding to conduct it.
Author: Dr. Pamela Kroft
ImageAlt: A researcher looking at charts and graphs

Title: Area Woman Discovers Meditation App Just Playing 'Shh' Sound On Loop For 30 Minutes
Subtitle: Premium subscription tier reportedly upgrades to 'Shhhhh' with whale sounds for $14.99 a month
Body:
SEATTLE — Local marketing director and self-described "wellness enthusiast" Jessica Tremblay, 38, announced Thursday that after six months of daily use of the mindfulness app CalmPresence Pro, she has concluded that the app's most popular 30-minute guided meditation is, in its entirety, someone saying "shh" into a microphone at gradually decreasing volumes.

"I thought I was just really bad at noticing the nuance," said Tremblay, who paid $89.99 for an annual subscription. "Like maybe I wasn't mindful enough to appreciate the full content. Turns out it's just 'shh' for half an hour."

A spokesperson for CalmPresence Pro confirmed the audio is "exactly as described" and disputed characterizations of it as "just shushing," noting that the sound is "intentionally crafted to signal to your nervous system that it should, and I'm quoting our wellness science team here, chill out."

"Our users report a 43% reduction in stress. We don't specify what they're stressed about or how we measured it, but the number is very comforting." — CalmPresence Pro spokesperson

The app currently has 4.8 stars and 200,000 reviews, the majority of which describe it as "life-changing" and "so peaceful." Tremblay has renewed her subscription.
Author: The Bunion Staff
ImageAlt: A woman with headphones in, eyes closed, presumably meditating
